full_judgment:
7. Mr. Ahmed Nawshad Zamir, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr. M. Ashraf Ali, the learned Advocates for the opposite-parties submit that the suit was filed by the present petitioner as the plaintiff for partition and khas possession on the basis of the document obtained from one Moslema as a minor through her uncle, who executed the sale deed dated 17-1-1983 regarding 3 decimals of land, therefore, the said transaction was not lawful as claimed by the plaintiff-petitioner partition of the suit land is not sustainable under the provision of law, therefore, the Rule should be discharged. 

 9. Considering the above submissions made by the learned Advocates and also considering the revisional application filed under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure along with the annexures therein, in particular, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate Court below and also considering the materials in the lower court records, it transpires to me that the present petitioner, namely Nurun Nahar as the plaintiff filed the title suit for partition and recovery of khas possession upon the land in plot No. 5002 by two sale deeds dated 12-12-1982 and 17-1-1983 from one Nazmul Hassan and Sahanaz Bilkis respectively from the land measuring 1 decimal and 3 decimals of land respectively. The total land 4 decimals was mutated in her name and she has been possessing the land but the present defendant dispossessed her from 3 decimals for which she was dispossessed even after an interim order of injunction granted by the Court. Accordingly, the suit for partition and recovery of khas possession was filed.
